propositions: CodeQL workflow originally ran on every push to main plus weekly; after removing push trigger, weekly cron became the primary scan of newly-landed code rather than a backstop for advisories, leaving SAST findings potentially unscanned for up to 7 days

Operator decision: CodeQL must move to 6-hourly cadence to restore intended coverage; the 28x cost argument does not apply because navapbc/rebar is public and CodeQL/Actions minutes are free for public repos
CodeQL is scheduled for 35 */6 * * * with distinct off-the-hour minute staggering against test.yml (41), optionality.yml (47), and verify-identity.yml (53)

CodeQL retains no push trigger and workflow_dispatch; it cannot join the push-preservation test cohort so test coverage must separate schedule-only cadence assertions from push-preservation assertions
The stale header comment asserting CodeQL deliberately avoids the 6-hourly tick and citing cost savings must be removed and rewritten to reflect the new rationale
